question: to the Commission Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing continues to present a serious threat to the sustainability of Mediterranean marine ecosystems as well as to the income and safety of European fishers. Repeated instances of fishing activities carried out by non-EU vessels in the maritime zones of Member States are causing particular concern. These instances raise serious questions about compliance with the international law of the sea and protection of the sovereign rights of Member States. In the Mediterranean there have been repeated complaints about fishing activities being carried out by non-EU vessels, including Turkish vessels, in areas where European fishers operate. The situation is creating conditions of unfair competition and is increasing tensions at sea. These instances undermine the effectiveness of European policy on combatting illegal fishing and test the zero tolerance policy proclaimed by the Union. In view of the above: 1.

Has the Commission recorded any instances of illegal or non-compliant fishing activities by non-EU vessels, including Turkish vessels, within the maritime zones of EU Member States in the Mediterranean?
What specific EU-wide measures does the Commission take or is it intending to take when there are repeated infringements by non-EU fishing vessels operating in areas of European interest?

Does the Commission intend to consider introducing stricter surveillance and control mechanisms and potential trade restrictions for countries that do not ensure compliance of their fishing fleets with international and European rules against illegal fishing?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) 1. Member States are in charge of fisheries control in their waters. The Commission receives and assesses sightings reports transmitted by Member States on alleged non-compliant fishing activities by third-country vessels in the Mediterranean. They are examined with the support of the European Fisheries Control Agency (EFCA) where relevant. 2. The EU has a comprehensive framework to address such situations, in particular Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009 on fisheries control1 and Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 on Illegal Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) fishing2. Member States have responsibilities as coastal States, including for surveillance, reporting and, where applicable, transmission to the flag State. Where sufficient information is available, the Commission may request the flag State to investigate and report on the outcome. 3. The Commission will continue to assess the information received and to use the tools available under EU and international rules where the legal conditions are met. The IUU Regulation already provides for cooperation with third countries and, where appropriate, for the identification of non-cooperating third countries and related trade measures. Any such step must be based on substantial evidence and its comprehensive assessment.
